ambiguities.text: The phrase 'all but one 64th' for gas allocation could be interpreted differently in edge cases with very low gas amounts.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume integer division is used: max_call_gas = gas - (gas // 64). For gas < 64, child receives (63 * gas) // 64 which rounds down.

ambiguities.text: The specification mentions 'extra_gas' without defining exactly what costs are included in this value for each opcode.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume extra_gas includes all fixed costs associated with the call (base cost, memory expansion, etc.) before the 63/64 allocation is calculated.

implicit_assumptions.description: All Ethereum clients implement the exact same gas calculation formula to maintain consensus.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Different gas calculations would cause chain splits as clients disagree on transaction validity.

implicit_assumptions.description: The new gas costs adequately price the actual computational/IO cost, preventing attackers from causing disproportionate resource usage.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If gas costs are still too low relative to actual resource usage, DoS attacks remain economically viable.

implicit_assumptions.description: Existing contracts that relied on precise gas calculations for CALL operations may behave differently after the fork.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Contracts using tight gas calculations (e.g., msg.gas - X for subcalls) may fail unexpectedly after the fork.

implicit_assumptions.description: The 8 MB per block data read limit is sufficient to prevent disk I/O based DoS attacks.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If actual disk I/O costs exceed estimates, nodes could still be DoS'd with the new gas prices.
